newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler not satisfied after profit rebound.
newsitem.headline: Daimler not satisfied after profit rebound.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG, which reported a convincing rebound to profitability in 1996, is still not satisfied with its financial performance, Chairman Juergen Schrempp said on Wednesday.
Speaking at a ceremony at the opening of an engine plant, Schrempp said 1996 group net profit of 2.8 billion marks ($1.6 billion) was "considerable, but not yet satisfying profit."
Daimler, Germany's largest company, reported a record 5.7 billion mark loss in 1995 after taking write-off charges associated with a massive overhaul of the company's opertions.
Schrempp said Daimler still needed to reduce costs and improve its inovational ability in order to lift profits.
The Daimler chairman said more flexible employment models, working groups and a new remuneration system were important steps in making the group more competitive.
Daimler had previously said it was not yet fully happy with last year's profits. Each operating unit in the group faces a goal of achieving 12 percent return on capital employed.
